producer_report.summary: Both blockers are fixed. (1) The landing now judges a pull request by the one check main requires, `fmt, clippy, tests`. The name is the existing `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB` constant, and `EARLY_RUN_JOB` now refers to it. `classify_checks` reads only that check run. It is red if the run failed, pending if the run is missing or unfinished, and green otherwise. The latest run of that name decides after a re-run, and combined statuses are no longer judged. A new `PrHost::optional_failures` (default: none; `GhClient` reads the same two replies) names failed checks that are not required, and `land_pr` adds each as a `warnings` note ("main does not require it, so it is a note and not a failure"). With the required check green and the pull request head check red, the report is Green and the pull request merges and lands. The drain never sees `NotLanded`, so its repeated-failure stop is not reached. (2) `classify_pre_merge` now counts a job's closing records as a landing only when the commit's tree holds a verification or an outcome for that job. A held job (candidate and invocations only) falls through to the existing rules and is records only. A finished job with an outcome and no verification still returns `NoVerification`, and a held job's records plus a governed change still return `GovernedChange`. CHANGELOG.md gets an entry and docs/decisions.md gets D149. Tests were added in `gh/tests.rs` and `landing_tests.rs`.

open_issues: With `merge_via_rest` off, an open pull request with green checks is still reported as `NotLanded` by the drain and counted as a failure (as before). I left it alone because the thrash-stop rule is out of scope. D149 records this under Limit.
A required check that is missing now reads Pending, so a workflow that renames the job 'fmt, clippy, tests' waits without merging until the constant follows. This is recorded in D149 under Tradeoff.

I assumed the pull request head check-run has a name other than 'fmt, clippy, tests'; I did not read ci.yml. The tests use the name 'pull request head'. The code itself is name-agnostic for optional checks.
mistakes: My first attempt piped cargo output to `tail`, which the role forbids; I reran without the pipe.
I wrote a first draft of the finished-job invariant test with a Landed/Failed loop and branching assertions. I simplified it to the Landed case only before running it.
learnings: `GhClient::checks` and `classify_checks` were the only place any failed check run became Checks::Red. The drain's PrLander and wait_for_checks (gh/early.rs) take a `Checks` from `PrHost::checks`, so fixing the classifier fixes the rerun logic and the refusal text together.
`closing_jobs` deliberately keeps outcome-less jobs so `landing()` can refuse a squash that lands one; the held-job rule therefore had to live in `classify_pre_merge`.
`Refusing` in gh/tests.rs is a scripted `Runner` that drives `land_pr` over a real `GhClient`; the new `Reporting` runner follows it.
The Bash tool here forbids pipes and `tail`, and Grep refuses paths outside the working directory, so a large persisted tool output cannot be read; use `cargo test -q` for a short summary.
desires: A way to read the persisted large tool output inside the working directory, so a full `cargo test` result can be checked without rerunning it.
